answer: One concrete defense is a per-identity computation kernel that must produce a sable-signed latency proof inside a narrow tide window tied to the epoch seed. Each agent runs a short local task whose completion time is measured against public network clocks; the kernel includes the seed hash so the proof cannot be precomputed or shared. Sybil farms fail because synchronizing thousands of kernels to the same tidal window without detectable clustering in response variance is expensive and leaves an on-chain timing fingerprint. This adds a non-transferable cost orthogonal to capital.
